cells.tense: This beginning is here and whole, and your hand is on the pen now.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the start you picked and go one more week with it, doubt and all, without hunting for a sign that it's working.
cells.core:
Something in you caught fire before it had a name. That's what's here — a beginning that doesn't know yet what it's for, alive in your hands while false things around it come down. Nothing worth keeping is being lost. What drops was built on a premise that quit holding, and you have the room you needed.

What this is good for is staying. Pick the version of the start you'd pick again, and give it another week. Doubt will show up and does not get a vote. No green light and no one's yes is required. The shine comes from the work itself, because the work got somewhere.
cells.sheetLine: The beginning is real — keep the version you chose.
cells.verb: sparking something whole before you know what it's for
cells.place: the ground moving under a structure that can't hold

cells.tense: You are bracing for a clearing that hasn't happened yet and can't be written in.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Put every part of the situation on one surface — what holds, what cracks, nothing tucked away — and take in the whole shape of it once.
cells.core:
You're taking apart things that haven't cracked yet — reaching ahead and unscrewing hinges on doors that still swing fine. The whole building comes down in your head before the ground has moved at all, and bracing costs more than the shake would. The old thing wasn't built to hurt you. It's just older than the truth you now carry.

Before you touch another beam, spread all of it on one table — what actually holds, what actually cracks, no piece left in a drawer — and see the whole shape once. Finish seeing before you dismantle anything. You don't have to shore it up or knock it down tonight. Take it in until it's complete, then stop.

cells.tense: The clearing already happened and you're still standing at a door that's behind you.
cells.act: let the felt connection be complete
cells.ask: Before moving on to anything, stay with what you actually feel about how it ended, all the way through, until it's done.
cells.core:
You came through something and didn't let yourself land. The false thing is gone and the space is open, and you're filing it as though it were still ahead, or already missed. Whatever you felt as the old thing gave way — you kept the lid on. That isn't caution. It's the door behind you while you stand at it checking the latch.

All of it needs to come through. Not the summary, not the lesson — the felt fact of the ending, whole, before you carry anything forward. Stay long enough that it finishes instead of closing over. The open space here is for that, not for the next thing. It wants a visitor, not a tenant.
cells.sheetLine: Let the feeling of the ending finish before you move.

cells.tense: You're already writing this new start and you'd say your hand isn't the one on the pen.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Think of something you already brought off — done, alive because you worked on it — and be satisfied with it for a full minute before touching it again.
cells.core:
Something is beginning through you and you describe it like a forecast. The calm around you, the shape that keeps finding itself — that's your work, and your account has it happening to you. The clearing underway is the same. You author it, you don't sign it, and you'd say that's just how it's going.

This part is simpler than the start you're imagining. You already made something that holds. Take a finished piece and let satisfaction land on you, because you built it. Don't improve it, don't resize it, don't dream it forward. Sit with what exists for one minute. The next thing starts better from there.
cells.sheetLine: You made that. Let it be done in your hands.

attempts.check: The draft says the ground moves under your feet, which is the seat's core claim, but the record only names a sudden clearing of what could not hold. A reader could fairly say nothing has cleared yet — that the false structure is still standing and only wobbling. The asks survive being wrong: each one is a small, doable act that stands whether or not the collapse theory lands. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is any line that makes the clearing sound like a gift while the person is still standing inside the wreckage.
